page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Page number and running head at the top, above the text. No margin notes. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Vicini arborem ita terra Titij.) Sequitur II: Eius quæq; arbor est, cuius in solo magnam radicum partem obtinet. L. si plures.6.D.arb.furt.L.ult.D. quod ui aut clam.

Prope confinium arbor posita.) Sequitur III: Arbor propè confinium posita, si in vicini fundum radices egerit, communis est.L.adeò.7. in fi.D. eod. Hac partitione responsum hoc idcirco non incommodè explicatum arbitror, quia neque plures, ut opinor, neque pauciores eius partes ostendi possunt. Hactenus quâ Grammaticâ, & quam

page.notes: The running head is a decorative line of display type; I could not read its words. The top line reads "L. si suprà" as printed, with the long s as "f" and "fi" read as "si". "Haetenus" in the printed text is a ligature "ct" that I read as Hactenus. The catchword "item" sits at the lower right, below the last full line, and is not repeated in the text. The marginal-style italic openings are run-in in the text block and are kept as paragraph openings, not headings.
